prs.title: Tags of your own, sorted by Sift

card.what: Each organization now gets its own tag list in Org settings, with six starter tags and add, rename, merge, retire, and restore actions. When an admin adds a tag or presses Find items, Sift checks the org's existing items and adds the tag automatically at 85% confidence or more, or suggests it at 60–85% for members to review on the tag page.
card.impact: Teams can manage their own tagging vocabulary and have existing items tagged automatically, and agents' unrecognized tags become suggestions rather than leaving entries stuck in Unplaced.

prs.title: To review: only the row you settle slides out, at once

card.what: On a tag's To review tab, adding or dismissing a suggestion now removes only that row, sliding it out and closing the gap immediately while the other rows stay usable. The write runs in the background and the page refreshes without showing a loading state.
card.why: Adding one suggestion turned every row's button to "Adding…", was slow, and made the page flash through its loading state, as reported by the owner.
card.impact: Reviewing suggestions on a tag feels fast and stable, since only the row being acted on changes and a refused suggestion returns with a reason. Under reduced motion the row simply disappears.

prs.title: To review: a checkmark confirmation when you add or dismiss

card.what: Adding or dismissing one of Sift's suggestions now shows a confirmation toast with a checkmark at the bottom of the screen, reading "Added latency to “…”" or "Dismissed latency for “…”", as the row slides out. If the action is refused, the row returns along with the error.
card.why: Adding or dismissing a suggestion should be confirmed the way every other write is, based on the owner's review of #182.
card.impact: People get immediate feedback that their add or dismiss action was applied, and they see the row restored if it failed.

prs.title: Hosting providers: Vercel, Render, Netlify, Fly.io — backend + Org settings › Hosting + Repo › Hosting (#97–#101)

card.what: Ships a unified hosting provider interface with Vercel (install or token), Render (API key), Netlify (OAuth or token), and Fly.io (read-only token), plus an Org settings > Hosting page for setup, environment parts, and provider connections. The repo dashboard's Usage tab gains a Hosting section showing each part's last deploy, recent deploy history, and traffic or CPU/memory usage. Hosting data is polled on the repo cron, and Vercel deploy webhooks trigger an immediate poll.
card.why: The PR lands work for issues #97 through #101 on main and supersedes #107, adding the screens that previously existed only on a local branch.
card.impact: Teams can connect their hosting providers and see deploy status and resource usage for every part of a repo in one place, while Cloudflare and Railway appear as legacy parts alongside them.
